facts.statement: The genus Brodavis was first described and named by Larry D. Martin, Evgeny N. Kurochkin, and Tim T. Tokaryk in 2012.
facts.quote: It was first described and named by Larry D. Martin, Evgeny N. Kurochkin and Tim T. Tokaryk in 2012

facts.statement: Brodavis was assigned to a new monogeneric family called Brodavidae.
facts.quote: assigned to a new monogeneric family, Brodavidae

facts.statement: Brodavis is a genus of freshwater birds belonging to the order Hesperornithiformes.
facts.quote: Brodavis is a genus of freshwater hesperornithiform birds

facts.statement: Fossils of Brodavis are known from the Late Cretaceous, possibly the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages, in North America and Asia.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous (possibly Campanian and Maastrichtian stage) of North America and Asia

facts.statement: The type species Brodavis americanus is known from a holotype left metatarsal collected in the Maastrichtian-age Frenchman Formation of Canada.
facts.quote: The type species, B. americanus, is known from the holotype left metatarsal, RSM P 2315.1 which was collected in the Maastrichtian-age Frenchman Formation of Canada

facts.statement: Brodavis baileyi is known from a holotype left metatarsal collected in the Maastrichtian-age Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota, dated between 66.8 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: B. baileyi is known from the holotype left metatarsal, UNSM 50665, which was collected in the Maastrichtian-age Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota, United States (dated to between 66.8 and 66 Ma ago)

facts.statement: Brodavis mongoliensis is known from a holotype left metatarsal collected in the Maastrichtian-age Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: B. mongoliensis is known from the holotype left metatarsal, PIN 4491-8, which was collected in the Maastrichtian-age Nemegt Formation of Mongolia

facts.statement: Brodavis varneri was originally named as a species of Baptornis by James Martin and Amanda Cordes-Person in 2007.
facts.quote: B. varneri was originally named as a second species of Baptornis by James Martin and Amanda Cordes-Person in 2007

facts.statement: It is debated whether Baptornis varneri represents a fourth species of Brodavis or belongs to a separate genus.
facts.quote: "Baptornis" varneri might represent a fourth species of Brodavis or belong to a separate genus

facts.statement: Brodavis is considered the first freshwater species and the latest known record of the order Hesperornithiformes.
facts.quote: Brodavis is considered to be the first freshwater and latest record of the order Hesperornithiformes

facts.statement: While hesperornithiforms likely lost flight by the end of the Early Cretaceous, minimal bone density in Brodavis suggests the possibility of some flying ability.
facts.quote: Although hesperornithiforms probably lost their flight abilities by the end of the Early Cretaceous, minimal pachyostosis in Brodavis suggests the possibility of some volant abilities

facts.statement: Brodavis lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
